title: The Letter of the Marlowe Estate
premise: Ada Blackwood, coroner of the fading town of Marlowe's Bend, is paid a suspiciously large retainer by a stranger to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a murder the client insists is already written into the town's future. When a body surfaces exactly as described, Ada realizes her anonymous client may be the killer, taunting her with foreknowledge of a crime only someone with access to official records could plan. As she traces the leak through decades of sealed estate files from the Marlowe family, she uncovers an old injustice the town buried: a wrongful conviction that destroyed an innocent family. In the end, Ada must choose between exposing the truth through legal channels — which would free a guilty heir protected by the town's founding families — or letting the vigilante client complete their revenge; she chooses a third path, trapping the killer publicly while forcing the courts to reopen the old case, at the cost of her own position and her last illusions about the law.
about_author: Xanthe Quintana is the pen name of a former rural records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing probate files in county basements before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, small-town complicity, and the people history forgets to bury properly.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Ada Blackwood's POV. A well-dressed stranger arrives at the coroner's office with a cash retainer and one request: prove that a murder will not happen. The date he names is three weeks away. Ada, proud of closing every case, accepts against her instincts. Beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Ada walks the cemetery at dawn, establishing her intimate knowledge of Marlowe's Bend and its dead. She catalogs recent deaths, finding nothing matching the stranger's description of the victim-to-be. Beat: quiet competence masking the first flicker of dread.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She tries to return the money; the client's lawyer refuses it, citing contract terms she never signed but somehow agreed to. The payment trail leads to a shell company tied to the old Marlowe Estate. Beat: the sense of being handled.

chapters.title: The First Discrepancy
chapters.summary: Ada notices the stranger knew details of an autopsy report never made public. Only four people had access. She begins a private list. POV shifts briefly to Deputy Cora Voss, who watches Ada ask odd questions. Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: Marlowe House
chapters.summary: Ada visits the decaying Marlowe Estate, now a museum nobody visits. A docent mentions the family archive was sealed after the 1987 trial. Ada requests access and is refused within the hour — too fast for anyone to have read her request. Beat: invisible walls.

chapters.title: The Body That Wasn't Yet
chapters.summary: A drifter is found dead in the river, matching the client's description almost perfectly — except the date is early. Ada performs the autopsy and finds evidence staged post-mortem. Someone rehearsed this death. Beat: horror sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: Cora's Doubts
chapters.summary: Deputy Voss's POV. Cora covers the drifter case as accidental drowning, under pressure from the sheriff. She suspects Ada knows more. Their uneasy alliance forms over bad coffee. Beat: two women circling the same lie from opposite sides.

chapters.title: The 1987 File
chapters.summary: Ada pulls the microfilm of the Marlowe murder trial: a housekeeper, Ruth Okafor, convicted of killing patriarch Edmund Marlowe. The evidence reads thin even thirty years later. Ruth died in prison. Her son vanished. Beat: grief for a stranger.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada interviews elderly residents who all repeat the same polished story of 1987 — too identical, like a script. One widow lets slip that Ruth had an alibi no one would hear. Beat: the weight of collective silence.

chapters.title: The Client Calls
chapters.summary: An untraceable call: the client notes the drifter was 'only a rehearsal' and warns Ada not to stand between him and justice. He quotes her own autopsy language back at her. Beat: violation — he is inside her work.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Ada narrows the leak: the retired sheriff, the current sheriff, the estate's trustee, or Cora. She tests each with false information, marking which version resurfaces. Beat: cold strategy replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs Wrong
chapters.summary: The false detail comes back — via the retired sheriff, Hollis Grange. But when Ada confronts him, he's terrified, not guilty: someone has been blackmailing him for years with his own 1987 mistakes. Beat: the list breaks open.

chapters.title: Ruth's Son
chapters.summary: Ada traces Ruth Okafor's son, Daniel, presumed dead — actually living under another name two counties over. He disappeared the week the retainer was paid. Is he the client, or the next victim? Beat: hope and suspicion entangled.

chapters.title: Estate of Secrets
chapters.summary: Ada breaks into the Marlowe archive at night and finds Edmund's real will, hidden from probate: it left everything to Ruth, acknowledging their affair and their son. The motive for the original murder inverts entirely. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Introduce Vivian Marlowe, the polished great-niece who controls the trust and funds half the town. Charming, generous, and present at every turn of Ada's investigation just a step ahead. Beat: admiration curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Second Date Approaching
chapters.summary: The client's named date is four days out. Police presence increases; the sheriff announces the drifter case closed. Ada realizes the real target is still unknown — the description fits several townspeople. Beat: ticking clock, widening dread.

chapters.title: Cora's Choice
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. She finds Ada's copied archive pages and must decide: report her, or help. She brings a box of her own — her father was a juror in 1987 and drank himself to death over his vote. Beat: loyalty shifting sides.

chapters.title: The Alibi Nobody Heard
chapters.summary: Ada locates the suppressed alibi witness, now in a care home: Ruth was with her the night Edmund died. The witness was paid to recant — by Hollis Grange, on instructions he never named. Beat: the old case cracks wide.

chapters.title: Date Night
chapters.summary: The client's date passes. No murder. Instead, every courthouse record of the 1987 trial vanishes overnight — stolen or destroyed. The client isn't killing a person; he's killing the cover-up. Or so he wants her to believe. Beat: relief laced with deeper wrongness.

chapters.title: Vivian's Invitation
chapters.summary: Vivian invites Ada to dinner at Marlowe House, disarmingly candid about the family's sins — except one. She warns Ada that Daniel Okafor is dangerous and shows her a threatening letter. Is it genuine, or planted? Beat: seduction of the reasonable enemy.

chapters.title: Daniel Found
chapters.summary: Ada confronts Daniel. Broken, angry, he denies being the client — but admits he came home to dig up his mother's case and found someone else had gotten there first, leaving him threatening notes in his own handwriting style. Beat: sympathy without certainty.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: Ada compares documents: the notes to Daniel, the retainer letter, and a 1987 confession signed by Ruth — likely coerced. The loops and pressure patterns point to someone taught to write like Ruth. Someone raised on her letters. Beat: forensic intimacy.

chapters.title: Hollis Breaks
chapters.summary: Hollis Grange, freed from blackmail by the stolen records, confesses to Ada: he buried the alibi in '87 because the Marlowe trust owned his debts. He never knew who gave the orders. He gives her a name redacted from his memory — a child's nickname. Beat: the past demanding interest.

chapters.title: Who Taught You to Write
chapters.summary: Ada realizes the client learned Ruth's hand because Ruth was raising him — meaning the client is connected to the estate household itself. She re-examines the museum staff roster and finds a name that shouldn't be there. Beat: the ground tilts.

chapters.title: The Docent
chapters.summary: The quiet estate docent, Elias Wren, is Ruth's nephew, raised in the servants' wing after her conviction. Confronted, he doesn't deny it — he hands Ada a full dossier: every document proving the conspiracy, collected over twenty years. Beat: the client revealed, and more sympathetic than feared.

chapters.title: His Case File
chapters.summary: Elias explains: he didn't hire Ada to stop a murder. He hired her to make the town watch one being prevented — to force the truth into daylight through her incorruptible reputation. The 'victim' was always meant to be himself. Beat: devastating reframe of the entire premise.

chapters.title: But Someone Else Read It
chapters.summary: Ada realizes the staged drifter death wasn't Elias — someone used his plan as camouflage. The real killer is eliminating everyone who can reopen the case, starting with witnesses. The alibi witness in the care home is next. Beat: race against a second, hidden clock.

chapters.title: Care Home Fire
chapters.summary: They arrive minutes late; the witness survived, barely, pulled out by an orderly. The arson points to a professional. Cora recognizes the method from an unsolved file — the same hand that killed Edmund Marlowe may still be alive. Beat: the past is not past.

chapters.title: Edmund's Killer
chapters.summary: Reconstructing 1987: Edmund was killed by his business partner's son — now the town's beloved judge, Marcus Hale — who framed Ruth to protect his inheritance and has guarded the secret ever since. Hale signed off on sealing the estate archive. Beat: the banality of respected evil.

chapters.title: Judge Hale
chapters.summary: Ada meets Hale openly, playing naive, and watches him lie beautifully. He offers her Hollis's old deal: her career for her silence. She accepts — aloud. Cora, listening from the next room, is horrified. Beat: Ada crosses her own line to buy time.

chapters.title: Falling
chapters.summary: Hale moves first: Ada is suspended for evidence tampering, Elias arrested for the arson, Daniel detained as a flight risk. Everything they built unravels in forty-eight hours. Beat: despair, the long dark night.

chapters.title: What Cora Kept
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. She reveals her father's jury notes, hidden for decades, showing the deliberation was rigged by a phone call from Hale's father. Cora chooses truth over the badge she loves. Beat: loyalty resolved into courage.

chapters.title: The Second Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Ada finds the pattern: both staged deaths were rehearsals of how Hale's father killed Edmund. The killer — Hale's fixer, the shell company's face — is completing the ritual, and the final performance requires a body in the Marlowe House study. Beat: location locked, clock final.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Ada proposes the unthinkable: let Elias 'escape' custody and hide in Marlowe House, exactly where the fixer expects him. Cora and Daniel rig the estate with recording equipment and witnesses. Beat: terrible hope, hands shaking.

chapters.title: Night at Marlowe House
chapters.summary: The trap springs. The fixer comes for Elias; Ada steps out of the dark instead, trading confessions recorded on every device in the room. The fixer nearly kills her before Cora's team floods in. Beat: climax — violence, terror, and the click of a running recorder.

chapters.title: Confession, Witnessed
chapters.summary: Hale arrives to clean up personally and walks into a room full of deputies, journalists tipped by Elias, and his own fixer's recorded testimony naming him. His composure finally cracks. Beat: justice arriving not through law, but in front of it.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Hale and the fixer are charged; the 1987 verdict is vacated; Ruth Okafor's name is cleared posthumously. Ada's suspension stands — she broke rules and knows it. The town that shunned her now needs her forgiveness. Beat: victory with a bitter finish.

chapters.title: The Refund
chapters.summary: Ada returns the retainer to Elias, who asks what she'll do now that she can't be a coroner here. She admits she never wanted invisibility — she wanted to matter. He offers her the estate archive to curate. Beat: belonging offered where isolation once lived.

chapters.title: Ruth's Stone
chapters.summary: The town gathers as a new headstone is laid for Ruth Okafor beside her son's chosen plot. Ada reads the corrected record aloud. Daniel stands at her shoulder. Beat: mourning turned to restoration.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name, Again
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ada's POV. She walks the cemetery at dawn one last time, adding a new grave to her mental map — the fixer's, unnamed and unmourned — and reflects that justice outside the law still leaves scars inside it. She stays in Marlowe's Bend, no longer invisible. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
